**Direction and Shape:**

So the overall pattern is:
- Very negative in winter months (Jan-Feb-Mar)
- Rising through spring
- Positive and relatively stable through summer/fall (May through November)
- Peak seems around September (month 9) or November (month 11)
- Drop again in December

This is a non-monotonic pattern - it rises from winter through spring, stays positive in summer/fall, then dips again in December. The shape is like an inverted U but with the low on the left (winter) and high in the middle-to-late months.

**Peak:** The peak contribution appears to be around month 9 (September) or month 11, where the upper range of SHAP values reaches about +0.25-0.27.

**Importance:** Ranked 5th out of 9 features - moderate importance.

**Key observations:**
- January has the most strongly negative effect (around -0.65 to -0.70)
- The transition from negative to positive happens around April-May
- Summer months (5-10) are generally positive
- December shows a return to negative values for many hours

The shape is non-monotonic - it rises from January to peak months (around Sept/Oct), then falls back in December.

[EFFECT] Month has a strong non-monotonic effect on predicted demand. Winter months — especially January — heavily suppress rentals, with SHAP contributions as low as about −0.65. Demand rises through spring, turns positive from around May onward, and peaks in September before dipping sharply again in December.

[IMPORTANCE] Month is the 5th most important feature out of 9, placing it in the middle tier. It has a meaningful but not dominant influence on predicted demand, notably setting a very strong seasonal floor in January.

[RECOMMENDATION] Bike availability and staffing should be scaled up significantly for the late-summer and early-autumn period (roughly August–October) and scaled back in the deep winter months of January and February, when the model consistently predicts much lower demand regardless of other conditions.
